title: When should I start talking to kids about money?
content:
There's a question we hear all the time from parents, teachers, and community leaders: When should I start talking to kids about money?

The answer surprises most people: age three. Not because a three-year-old needs to understand compound interest. But because the habits that determine financial health — saving, goal-setting, patience, planning — are already forming in those earliest years. And habits, as any researcher will tell you, are far easier to build than to rebuild. That's the idea at the heart of Grow Good Daily.

The Gap Nobody Talks About

Financial stress touches nearly every family in America, across income levels and zip codes. Yet most children receive their first real money lesson sometime in high school — if at all. By then, the window for building deep, automatic habits has largely closed.

The research is clear: financial behaviors and attitudes take root early. Children who learn to save before they start school are measurably more likely to become savers as adults. Children who grow up in households where money is talked about openly — where goals are set, delayed gratification is practiced, and big dreams are encouraged — carry those patterns forward for life.

What's missing isn't information. It's early access. That's the gap Grow Good Daily exists to close.

A Whole-Community Approach

Most financial education programs target one audience — students in a classroom, or parents at a workshop. Grow Good Daily is built differently. It's a whole-community model, bringing early financial education to children, families, schools, and community organizations together.

Because the truth is, a child who learns about saving at school but never hears about it at home won't carry that lesson very far. And a parent who wants to raise financially capable kids but doesn't know where to start needs support too. Real, lasting change happens when the message is consistent — when the adults and institutions in a child's life are all speaking the same language.

That's what we're building: a coordinated, community-wide ecosystem that makes early financial education the norm, not the exception.

Start Early. Dream Big. Grow Good.

Our tagline isn't just a slogan. It's a sequence. Start early — because the earlier habits form, the stronger they stick. Financial confidence isn't built in a semester; it's built over a childhood.

Dream big — because financial education without ambition is just accounting. We want kids to connect money habits to their dreams — what they want to create, build, give, and become.

Grow good — because the goal was never just personal wealth. A child who learns to save, give, plan, and lead doesn't just improve their own life. They grow into someone who makes their community better.

What's Coming

Grow Good Daily is in its founding chapter. In the weeks and months ahead, we'll be sharing:

Research and insights on early childhood financial habits and what the data says about starting young Practical resources for parents, educators, and community leaders to bring these conversations to life — starting at age three

Stories from kids, families, and communities who are already growing good, every day Updates on our programs, partnerships, and the community we're building together

This is the beginning of something meaningful. We're glad you're here for it.

If you believe as we do, that every child deserves a strong financial foundation and the freedom to dream big, this community is for you.

Welcome to Grow Good Daily.

excerpt: Most children don't learn about money until it's too late to build real habits. Grow Good Daily explains why starting financial education at age 3 changes everything.
